subject.title: refactor(macos): move PortGuardian state to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw accept a native-runtime-only migration owner and fail-closed exclusion of older JSON-writing macOS copies for this one-way PortGuardian storage cutover?
rationale: This changes persistent host-global tunnel ownership across app versions; code review cannot determine whether the downgrade and mixed-copy support boundary is an acceptable product and security contract.

options.title: Accept the bounded native cutover
options.body: Approve the native migration exception and documented one-way mixed-version contract after current-head signed-app proof is attached.

options.title: Require a different upgrade contract
options.body: Keep compatibility through a maintainer-approved migration or operator-recovery path before replacing the old JSON ledger.

options.title: Pause the PortGuardian cutover
options.body: Defer this branch until the shared native-state dependency and storage ownership model are accepted together.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded native cutover
recommendation.body: Approve the native migration exception and documented one-way mixed-version contract after current-head signed-app proof is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: The author is the only concrete design owner identified in the supplied stacked migration history and has explicitly requested this contract decision.
